items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: I said, 'Well, I met Duke before,' which I had out in Chicago, back in the '60s.

ctx.x: the sound that he wanted to convey the message for.

Well, that was the music. You know that's what music is about, actually. You know, you're telling stories, you know, and you're painting pictures, and I can't explain it, but you hit it on the head; Duke hit it on the head. A lot of musicians know about that, just like we were playing when I was working with Flip as a youngster, musicians during that time were playing nightclubs, you were playing something and somebody might hit a sour note, a wrong note, and straining to reach it, and brush his shirt off like…

I was always partial to the blues (acoustic) ... but nowadays everything is so technical; you know, it seems like they don't want you to look at each other when you're playing, usually, unless you're up on a big concert stage, you know, when you're 25 feet away from each other, there is no closeness there.
